deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It continues a set of German notes on the ancient history of Syracuse, under the 4th period, 'From Dionysius I to the Roman capture, 405–212 BC'.

The content, paraphrased in order:
(1) Plato was summoned to the court of Dionysius II. Dion's influence on the young king did not last. The king became dissolute and tyrannical.
(2) Dion had to flee. He returned with a body of troops, took the city and finally the citadel.
(3) He wanted to give Syracuse a constitution that was too aristocratic (the interlinear word is hard to read). He met great resistance and was finally murdered by Callippus. The year is not given; it was 354 BC.
(4) In 346 Dionysius II regained power and raged worse than before.
(5) The Carthaginians used this moment to besiege Syracuse. The city found a rescuer in Timoleon of Corinth.
(6) Syracuse could not bear its good fortune for long. About 12 years after Timoleon's death (marked '+337'), Agathocles seized supreme power. He had all the virtues and faults of an adventurer. He was the son of a potter and rose through war, distinguished himself by courage, became general, and in 317 became king of Syracuse.

The page is a fair-copy lecture or school notebook on ancient history. Nothing is computed. The connection to Gauss is only archival (it sits in the bundle). The hand and content suggest student or lecture notes, possibly not by Gauss himself.
errors: Historical slip: the page says Agathocles took power 'about 12 years' after Timoleon's death (c. 337 BC). His seizure of power in 317/316 BC is about 20 years later.
The page gives no date for Dion's murder (354 BC). Read as written, the narrative is compressed but not wrong.
The original spelling 'Agatocles' is corrected in the manuscript itself to 'Agathocles' by an interlinear 'h'.

results.what: Narrative notes on Syracusan history: Dionysius II, Dion, Callippus, Timoleon, Agathocles
results.usually_credited_to: Standard classical sources (Diodorus Siculus, Plutarch's lives of Dion and Timoleon)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely historical narrative from a history notebook, with no mathematical content. It is likely not even in Gauss's own hand.

checkable.asserts: The interval between Timoleon's death (c. 337 BC) and Agathocles becoming ruler (317 BC) is about 20 years, not the 12 stated.
The length of the 4th period heading (405–212 BC) is 193 years (context check only).

transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Er kam allein sein Einfluss' reads more naturally as 'Allein sein Einfluss auf den jungen König dauerte nicht lange'. 'Ein' is an interlinear insertion above 'fluss'.
Line 6: the interlinear 'wenn[?] einer[?]' is uncertain. It is placed under 'der Stadt, und' and may read 'wieder'.

Line 7: the interlinear '+zu blutige+' is doubtful. In the image it looks like 'zu aristokratische' (or similar) inserted before 'Verfassung'. This is historically apt, since Dion aimed at an aristocratic constitution.

The sentence order is scrambled by the interlinear layout. The intended reading is: 'Er wollte Syracus eine zu [aristokratische] Verfassung geben. Allein er fand großen [Widerstand] und wurde endlich durch Callippus ermordet.'
'Feldherrn' is struck through and replaced by 'Abentheurers'; 'hatte' is struck in the next line ('Er sich durch Muth ausgezeichnet' is to be read as 'Er hatte sich…' or 'Er zeichnete sich…').
